PullRequest.Title: sessions: model a real effort and context size in the responsive picker fixture

Follow-up to #340359, which made the tabbed model picker the default.

## What changed

The `ResponsiveModelResizeCycle*` fixtures in `src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatInput.fixture.ts` gave their model an effort option labelled `Max 1M`. That label imitated the old picker's `Effort Context` readout. The tabbed picker's readout also shows a model's context window when it has no context-size setting, so the fixture rendered a confusing **`Max 1M · 132K`**. The `132K` is the fixture's 128K input + 4K output tokens.

The model now advertises:
- **Thinking effort:** a real `Max` level (`Low`, `Medium`, `High`, `Max`, default `Max`).
- **Context size:** a real setting (`128K` / `1M`, default `1M`).

The readout now reads **`Max · 1M`** at a similar width, so the resize cycles still squeeze both halves of the picker.

The `Compact` fixture's expected visual description also said "the model configuration remains visible". That was true of the old picker, but the tabbed picker hides the readout when compact, so the description now says it's hidden. That fixture's rendering is unchanged (same screenshot hash before and after).

Test-only change; no product code is touched.

## How to test

Run the Component Explorer and open `sessions/chat/input/chatInput/ResponsiveModelResizeCycle*`:

| Fixture | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Expanded | `Max 1M · 132K` | `Max · 1M` |
| Ellipsized | `Max 1M · 132K` (name truncated) | `Max · 1M` (name still truncated) |
| Compact | icon only, readout hidden | unchanged, same hash |
| Minimal | icon only, readout hidden | unchanged |

Validation run locally:
- Component Explorer `check_fixture_errors` on `^sessions/chat/input/chatInput/`: **28/28 OK**.
- Component Explorer `check_stability` on `^sessions/chat/input/chatInput/ResponsiveModel`: **8/8 stable**.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: **passed**.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatInput.fixture.ts`: **passed**.

None of these fixtures are in `test/componentFixtures/blocks-ci-screenshots.md`, so no committed baseline needs updating.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run any of the four sessions/chat/input ResponsiveModelResizeCycle component fixtures and settle on expanded, ellipsized, compact, or minimal width
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fixture registration supplies one in-memory model; renderChatInput constructs the local chat input, derives the two-value configuration summary, performs the pre-existing initial layouts, and executes the pre-existing 49 scheduled resize callbacks before the fixture settles. The added schema field is consumed synchronously as small local object/array scans on this path; no new asynchronous work blocks progress.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one model with two configuration properties and the unchanged fixed resizeWidths sequence (48 cycle widths plus one final width) per fixture; effective schema cardinality increases from one property to two, not with user data or repository size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing renderer schedules all fixed resize timers together but executes their layout callbacks at 16 ms offsets on the UI thread. The diff does not change timer count, parallelism, serialization, backpressure, or layout cardinality.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or cache key is introduced or bypassed. Configuration defaults are read from the same in-memory fixture metadata; cold and warm executions do the same bounded local work, with no negative-cache behavior or coalescing concern.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete diff and transitive renderer/configuration helpers show bounded in-memory schema lookup and DOM text generation only, with unchanged layout scheduling and no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, network, or serialization boundary introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact DOM/layout duration depends on the component-explorer host, but the diff adds only one constant-sized property and short labels while preserving the same model count and resize count; there is no realistically scaling input or boundary cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Compared with the prior fixture, the changed model summary scans two constant-sized properties instead of one and intentionally renders a second short readout; this does not add resize callbacks, external calls, unbounded allocation, retained state, or materially heavier synchronous UI work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Register and display the ResponsiveModelResizeCycleCompact fixture metadata in the Component Explorer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed expectedVisualDescriptions string is static fixture metadata used for visual expectation text; it does not alter renderChatInput or the compact resize/layout path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One replacement string for one fixture definition; cardinality is constant.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous work, queueing, or concurrency is added by the description change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache interaction or invalidation is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line is declarative metadata and the actual render callback is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the runtime difference is a small constant string replacement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance effect and no finding.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file, two-hunk diff and traced fixture rendering, model-configuration lookup/readout generation, storage-capable configuration code, and resize scheduling. The PR changes only test fixture metadata and one expected-description string. It preserves one-model cardinality, the fixed 49-resize schedule, concurrency, and all expensive-boundary counts; no performance finding or regression-fix record is warranted.
